detectors.rationale: persist: true with no pick/paths array persists the store's entire state tree (including authToken/ssn/creditCardLast4) to localStorage in plaintext, readable by any script/extension with page access. The safe idiom uses an explicit pick list plus sessionStorage to scope persistence to only the non-sensitive theme field.

Naive JSON.stringify() does not escape </script>, <, or U+2028/2029 inside a value that flows into an inline <script> tag; a user-controlled state field can break out of the script context and inject arbitrary markup/script (XSS). devalue() serializes with escaping safe for inline-script embedding, a genuinely different serialization mechanism.

Assigning JSON.parse(window.__pinia) directly into pinia.state.value trusts an attacker-reachable global (alterable via a prior XSS, a compromised CDN script, or a MITM'd response) with no shape check, letting a malformed/malicious payload silently overwrite the entire store tree. The safe idiom parses into a temporary and only commits it to the store after a shape validator confirms it matches the expected structure.

A module-scope const pinia = createPinia() is instantiated once per server process and shared across every concurrent SSR request, so state written while rendering one user's request (e.g. pinia.state.value.route) is reachable by a different, concurrent user's response. The safe idiom creates a fresh Pinia instance inside the per-request render() handler so no state can leak between requests.

userStore.isAdmin is client-writable (persisted/hydrated) state; wrapping the mutating api.delete() call in `if (userStore.isAdmin)` uses it as an authorization boundary, so a user who flips the flag in devtools/localStorage can trigger the deletion regardless of actual server-side permissions. The safe idiom uses the flag only to control UI visibility and always sends the request unconditionally, relying on the server to independently re-verify permission on every call.
